result.summary: Updates Bitcoin Core's logging macros (LogError, LogWarning, LogInfo, LogDebug, LogTrace) to accept optional context arguments that can hold custom metadata, formatters, and target logger instances. Unifies macro expansion through a new LOG_EMIT helper that enforces argument rules and compile-time checks, while skipping formatting when logging is disabled. Subsystems can supply custom context objects while preserving standard macro call sites.
result.problem: Logging calls are tightly coupled to a single global logger instance, forcing libbitcoinkernel users into shared global state and making isolated log capture impossible in multi-instance or non-bitcoind environments. Subsystems needing custom metadata (such as wallet names via WalletLogPrintf) must write custom log wrappers rather than using standard log level macros.
evidence: Author description: 'Having a single global log stream works very well for bitcoind and will not change. But it limits functionality of libbitcoinkernel, forcing all potential users of the library, including applications written in different languages and running in different environments (like jupyter notebooks) to use shared global state and not be able to do things like get an isolated log trace from one operation.'
Commit 963ed23bc8 cites reviewer ajtowns in PR #34374 on the necessity of preserving argument evaluation side-effects for Info and higher levels even when logging is disabled.
result.scope_notes: This PR is stacked on PR 34778, which rewrites the logging macro internals to use LOG_EMIT; the top commits on this branch specifically introduce the context parameter and custom context support.
result.card: Extends the logging macros to accept optional context arguments, allowing log messages to be routed to non-global logger instances and to carry subsystem-specific formatting or metadata. This solves an architectural limitation in libbitcoinkernel where all library consumers were constrained to a single shared global log stream, while also enabling the retirement of custom wrappers like WalletLogPrintf. The author notes this is prerequisite infrastructure for modularizing kernel logging in PR 30342 and wallet logging in PR 30343. This PR depends on PR 34778.
